judgment.rationale: A Ctrl+H shortcut mapping may also match Ctrl+Shift+H because Keyboard Manager's exact-match option defaults off. The report does not establish whether exact matching was enabled, so the key configuration must be clarified before treating this as an interception defect.
evidence: The issue title and report describe Keyboard Manager shortcut interception.
Current shortcut matching includes an optional exactMatch control, defaulting to false.
A Ctrl+H mapping can therefore intentionally match a shortcut that adds Shift unless exact matching is selected.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the exact source shortcut and exact-match setting; then compare the reported additional-modifier shortcut with that setting enabled.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current behavior may be the configured non-exact matching semantics; the issue does not yet show a failure when exact matching is enabled.

issue_context.summary: The shortcut-interception report may be explained by the current default that permits a mapping to match with additional modifiers.
known_information: The issue has no comments and no assignee.
Keyboard Manager exposes an exact-match option for shortcut mappings; it defaults to false.
A Ctrl+H mapping may match Ctrl+Shift+H when exact matching is disabled.
inferences: The described interception may be intended shortcut matching rather than a defect.
If exact matching was enabled and the extra-modifier shortcut is still intercepted, a separate matching issue remains possible.
issue_context.analysis: The first discriminating question is the configured exact-match state. A broad hook investigation or fix proposal would be premature until that option and the exact source/target chords are known.

comment.body: Keyboard Manager's shortcut matching allows extra modifiers when exact matching is off by default, so a Ctrl+H mapping may also intercept Ctrl+Shift+H. Could you share the exact source/target chords and whether the mapping's exact-match option is enabled? If it was off, please enable it and test the same chord; that result will tell us whether this is a configuration match or a separate interception issue.
